newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber closes lower, funds build long position.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber closes lower, funds build long position.

text.p: CME lumber futures finished lower as funds continued to build long positions amid bearish technicals and a sloppy cash market.
Dealers said Cargill Investor Services, a seller of September during the last few days, was again on the sell side. There was talk the selling was fund-related.
They noted that September's open interest had been climbing steadily and stood at 2,047 lots, as of July 22, up more than 300 lots since the end of last week.
Contract lows were established in September, March and May positions.
Dealers also noted a significant narrowing in September's premium to October, partly due to late buying by locals of the latter month.
September closed off $6.40 at $339.40 per thousand board feet after earlier setting a contract low of $339.20. Other months were down $0.90 to the $10.00 limit.
